name: MathlibAnnex.PluckerRecovery.LimitCertificate.image_unitBall_eq
title: The recovered contraction maps one unit ball onto the other

content.display_title: The recovered contraction maps one unit ball onto the other
content.one_sentence_role: Upgrades ball inclusion to equality by strict compact-subset volume comparison.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n=m+1>0$ and $V=\mathbb R^n$ with the reference sup norm and standard Lebesgue measure $\lambda$. The continuous norms $p,q$ have fixed positive comparison constants
$$a_p\|x\|_\infty\le p(x)\le b_p\|x\|_\infty,\qquad
a_q\|x\|_\infty\le q(x)\le b_q\|x\|_\infty.$$
Set $K_p=\{x:p(x)\le1\}$, $K_q=\{x:q(x)\le1\}$ and $v_p=\lambda(K_p)$, $v_q=\lambda(K_q)$, as positive finite real numbers. Let $L:V\to V$ be a real linear map with the following properties: $q(Lx)\le p(x)$ for every $x$, $L(K_p)\subseteq K_q$, $v_p|\det L|=v_q$, $\det L\ne0$, and $L$ is bijective. Then
$$L(K_p)=K_q.$$
content.assumptions: The two norm models and one already fixed real linear map $L$ with the seven displayed certificate properties are inputs. In particular, its ball inclusion and determinant-volume equation must concern the same $L$. Equality of Plücker bodies is not an input to this theorem.
content.conclusion: Every image of a $p$-unit-ball vector is in $K_q$, and every point in $K_q$ is such an image.
content.proof_summary: Compute the image volume for the same map and exclude a proper compact subset of the target unit ball.

proof_steps.text:
**Compute the volume of this same linear image.** The change-of-variables formula gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\lambda(L(K_p))
 &=|\det L|\lambda(K_p)\\
 &=|\det L|v_p\\
 &=v_q=\lambda(K_q).
\end{aligned}$$
Here the first equality is the [linear image-volume formula](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/360da6fa66c1273b76b6b2d8c5666fd5ac2e3b56/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/Lebesgue/EqHaar.lean#L313-L315), used with Lebesgue measure $\lambda$, the continuous linear map $L$, and the set $K_p$. The second uses $v_p=\lambda(K_p)$; the third uses the assumed identity $v_p|\det L|=v_q$. This is the [image-volume calculation](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/LimitRecovery.lean#L321-L327) for the map in the supplied certificate.

All volumes in this calculation are finite: $K_p,K_q$ are compact, $L$ is continuous, and Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets. We therefore identify these finite measures with the same nonnegative real numbers throughout. The resulting [equality of image and target measures](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/LimitRecovery.lean#L350-L357) concerns the same $L(K_p)$ and $K_q$ that occur in the inclusion hypothesis.

**Rule out a proper compact subset.** Continuity of $L$ makes $L(K_p)$ compact. If its known inclusion in $K_q$ were proper, [strict measure loss inside a seminorm ball](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Ball/VolumeRigidity.lean#L120-L149) would give
$$\lambda(L(K_p))<\lambda(K_q).$$
The inputs at this use are Lebesgue measure, continuous seminorm $q$, compactness of the subset, inclusion and inequality of the sets. The output contradicts Step 1. Thus $L(K_p)=K_q$. Equal measures of arbitrary sets alone would not justify equality.

content.lean_realization_notes: The norm comparisons provide compact unit balls and positive finite volumes. Every volume used in the proof is finite; no infinite measure is treated as a real number.
